text: Nearest-neighbour lookup has no gradient, so the decoder's gradient is copied straight to the encoder (the straight-through estimator ), and two extra terms train the codebook and keep the encoder near it: loss = reconstruction + ‖sg[z e ] − e‖ 2 + β ‖z e − sg[e]‖ 2 z e , e the encoder's vector at one position and its nearest codebook vector sg stop-gradient: the first term moves only the codebook (the codebook loss ), the second only the encoder (the commitment loss , β = 0.25 in the paper and here) def quantize(self, ze): # src/latent/vq.py B, D, H, W = ze.shape flat = ze.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).reshape(-1, D) E = self.codebook.weight d = flat.pow(2).sum(1, keepdim=True) - 2 * flat @ E.t() + E.pow(2).sum(1)[None] idx = d.argmin(1) zq = E[idx].view(B, H, W, D).permute(0, 3, 1, 2) return zq, idx.view(B, H, W) def forward(self, x): ze = self.ae.encode(x) zq, idx = self.quantize(ze) z_st = ze + (zq - ze).detach() # straight-through estimator return self.ae.decode(z_st), ze, zq, idx Read the library version critically: diffusers' VectorQuantizer keeps a known bug for backward compatibility, "due to a bug the beta term was applied to the wrong term" ( models/autoencoders/vae.py lines 574 to 576 and 651 to 654, v0.41.0 ): with the default legacy=True , β multiplies the codebook term and the commitment term gets weight 1.
